title: Psalms Chapter 57 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 57 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 57 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 57.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:1, where does David say he will make his refuge?
options: In the shadow of God's wings
questions.correctAnswer: In the shadow of God's wings
questions.explanation: David states that he will make his refuge in the shadow of God's wings, as found in Psalms 57:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:2, to whom does David cry?
questions.correctAnswer: God most high
questions.explanation: David says he will cry unto God most high, as stated in Psalms 57:2.

questions.question: What does God send from heaven according to Psalms 57:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:3 mentions that God shall send forth his mercy and his truth from heaven.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 57:4 describes David's soul as being among lions.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:4 states, 'My soul is among lions,' affirming that the statement is true.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:1, why does David ask God to be merciful to him?
options: Because his soul trusteth in God
Because he is in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because his soul trusteth in God
questions.explanation: David requests mercy because his soul trusteth in God, as shown in Psalms 57:1.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 57:6, those who prepared a net for David's steps fell into the pit themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 states that those who digged a pit before David fell into it themselves.

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:5, where does David want God to be exalted?
questions.correctAnswer: Above the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:5 says, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens.'

questions.question: What instruments does David mention awakening in Psalms 57:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Psaltery and harp
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:8 mentions the awakening of the psaltery and harp as part of David's praise.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 57:7 states that David's heart is fixed and he will sing and give praise.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:7 clearly states, 'My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.'

questions.question: In Psalms 57:4, what are the sons of men compared to?
questions.correctAnswer: Spears and arrows
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:4 describes the sons of men as having teeth like spears and arrows.

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:9, among whom will David praise the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: Among the people and nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:9 says David will praise the Lord among the people and sing among the nations.

questions.question: What does David say about God's mercy in Psalms 57:10?
options: It is great unto the heavens
It is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: It is great unto the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:10 states that God's mercy is great unto the heavens.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:3, what will God save David from?
options: The reproach of him that would swallow him up
questions.correctAnswer: The reproach of him that would swallow him up
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:3 states God will save David from the reproach of those who would swallow him up.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:11, what does David ask to be above all the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:11 requests that God's glory be above all the earth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 57:2, God performs all things for David.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:2 says God that performeth all things for David.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 57 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 57 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:5, how is God described in relation to the heavens and the earth?
options: God is exalted above the heavens and His glory above all the earth
God is hidden beneath the earth and silent in the heavens
God is equal to the heavens and the earth
God is only present in the heavens but not on earth
questions.correctAnswer: God is exalted above the heavens and His glory above all the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:5 clearly states, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth.' This emphasizes God's supreme position above both heaven and earth, a theme supported by similar exaltation in Psalms 57:11.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:6, what happens to those who have prepared a net and dug a pit for the psalmist?
options: They fall into the pit themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They fall into the pit themselves
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 states that those who prepared a net and dug a pit for the psalmist end up falling into it themselves, showing God's justice and protection. This idea of divine justice relates to the trust expressed in Psalms 57:1 and the steadfastness in Psalms 57:7.

questions.question: How does Psalms 57:7 describe the psalmist's heart in response to his circumstances?
options: Fixed on God with resolve to sing and give praise
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed on God with resolve to sing and give praise
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise,' indicating a firm trust in God despite adversity. This complements the refuge described in Psalms 57:1 and the call to exalt God in Psalms 57:5.

questions.question: What does the psalmist urge to 'awake' in Psalms 57:8, and what does this signify about his spiritual practice?
options: His glory, psaltery, and harp; signifying early praise and worship
His enemies; signifying a call to battle
The sun and moon; signifying natural order
His soul and body; signifying rest
questions.correctAnswer: His glory, psaltery, and harp; signifying early praise and worship
questions.explanation: The verse calls to 'Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp,' symbolizing the psalmist's commitment to praise God with music early in the morning, aligning with the fixed heart in Psalms 57:7 and trust in divine protection seen in Psalms 57:6.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is highlighted by the psalmist’s declaration in Psalms 57:7 to sing and give praise despite adversity?
questions.correctAnswer: Trust and steadfastness in God
questions.explanation: The psalmist's fixed heart and praise in Psalms 57:7 demonstrate trust and steadfastness in God even amid trials, consistent with seeking refuge in God (Psalms 57:1) and God's exaltation (Psalms 57:5).

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:6, what emotional state does the psalmist describe as a result of the enemies’ traps?
options: His soul is joyful and free
His soul is angry and vengeful
questions.correctAnswer: His soul is bowed down
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 says, 'my soul is bowed down,' indicating a state of heaviness or distress due to the enemies’ schemes, which contrasts with his resolve to praise God in Psalms 57:7 and trust in His exaltation in Psalms 57:5.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:5 teach about the relationship between God's glory and the earth?
options: God's glory should be above all the earth
God's glory is limited to the heavens
God's glory is hidden from the earth
God's glory only belongs to the chosen people
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory should be above all the earth
questions.explanation: The verse commands, 'let thy glory be above all the earth,' emphasizing God's universal glory over all creation, which supports the psalmist's trust and praise in Psalms 57:7 and the call for exaltation in Psalms 57:11.

questions.question: How does the imagery in Psalms 57:6 about enemies' traps relate to the psalmist’s confidence expressed in Psalms 57:7?
options: Despite enemies’ schemes, the psalmist remains fixed in praise
The psalmist gives in to fear and stops praising
The traps succeed in silencing the psalmist
questions.correctAnswer: Despite enemies’ schemes, the psalmist remains fixed in praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 describes enemies’ attempts to harm, yet Psalms 57:7 shows the psalmist's heart is fixed on God and he chooses to praise, illustrating faith and resilience despite adversity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:8 imply about the psalmist's daily spiritual discipline?
options: He rises early to worship God with music
He avoids music and worship in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: He rises early to worship God with music
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I myself will awake early,' along with calling musical instruments to awake, indicating a practice of early morning worship, reflecting dedication seen in Psalms 57:7 and trust in God’s protection in Psalms 57:6.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels overwhelmed by enemies’ schemes and doubts God’s protection. Based on Psalms 57:6-7, what biblical truth can you share?
options: Even when enemies prepare traps, God’s followers can fix their hearts on Him and praise Him
Enemies’ traps are always successful and God abandons His people
It is better to avoid God’s presence when in trouble
One should rely solely on personal strength to overcome enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Even when enemies prepare traps, God’s followers can fix their hearts on Him and praise Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 shows enemies’ attempts to harm, yet Psalms 57:7 encourages fixing the heart on God and praising Him despite adversity, offering comfort and guidance for believers under attack.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:5 teach about the attitude believers should have towards God's position in the universe?
options: Believers should exalt God above the heavens and all the earth
Believers should prioritize earthly things over God
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should exalt God above the heavens and all the earth
questions.explanation: The verse calls for God to be exalted above the heavens and His glory above all the earth, teaching believers to honor God's supreme authority, consistent with the psalmist's praise in Psalms 57:7-8.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 57:8, the psalmist plans to use the psaltery and harp to praise God early in the morning.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:8 states, 'Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early,' showing the psalmist’s commitment to early morning musical worship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:6 reveal about the fate of those who try to harm the psalmist?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 says that those who dig a pit for the psalmist fall into it themselves, indicating divine justice and protection.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 57:7 teaches that the psalmist’s heart is unstable and fearful in times of trouble.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:7 declares, 'My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed,' indicating stability and confidence, not fear or instability.

questions.question: How does Psalms 57:5 and Psalms 57:11 together teach about God’s glory?
options: God’s glory should be exalted above the heavens and all the earth
God’s glory is limited to a physical temple
God’s glory is only for the psalmist to see
God’s glory is hidden from the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God’s glory should be exalted above the heavens and all the earth
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 57:5 and 57:11 emphasize exalting God above the heavens and the earth, highlighting His universal glory accessible to all creation, reinforcing the psalmist’s trust and praise.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 57 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 57.

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:9, where will the psalmist praise the Lord?
options: In the cave where he fled
questions.correctAnswer: Among the people and nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:9 states, 'I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: I will sing unto thee among the nations,' indicating public and widespread praise.

questions.question: What two attributes of God are emphasized in Psalms 57:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:10 highlights God's 'mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds,' focusing on mercy and truth.

questions.question: Which phrase from Psalms 57:11 expresses a call for God's exaltation?
options: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens
I will sing and give praise
They have prepared a net for my steps
questions.correctAnswer: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:11 explicitly says, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: let thy glory be above all the earth,' calling for God's exaltation.

questions.question: In Psalms 57:7, what is the psalmist's heart described as?
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:7 says, 'My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise,' indicating steadfastness.

questions.question: What instruments does the psalmist mention awakening in Psalms 57:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Psaltery and harp
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:8 states, 'Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp,' referring to these instruments.

questions.question: What is the primary literary device evident in the repetition of 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens' in Psalms 57:5 and 57:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The repetition of this phrase at the beginning (v.5) and end (v.11) forms an inclusio, framing the psalm with a thematic emphasis on God's exaltation.

questions.question: How does Psalms 57:10's mention of 'mercy' and 'truth' extending to the heavens and clouds connect to Psalms 36:5?
options: Both describe God's steadfast love and faithfulness as boundless
Both focus on God's judgment against enemies
Both emphasize God's wrath and punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Both describe God's steadfast love and faithfulness as boundless
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:5 says, 'Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds,' paralleling Psalms 57:10's description of God's mercy and truth extending to the heavens and clouds.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by the psalmist's refuge 'in the shadow of thy wings' as seen in Psalms 57:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth 2:12
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:12 uses the phrase 'the wings of the LORD' as a metaphor for protection, closely echoing the refuge imagery in Psalms 57:1.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'Michtam' as it appears in the title of Psalms 57?
questions.correctAnswer: Golden poem or engraved poem
questions.explanation: The term 'Michtam' is traditionally understood to mean 'golden poem' or 'engraved poem,' indicating a precious or carefully composed psalm, as seen in Psalms 57's title.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of God's exaltation above all, similar to Psalms 57:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Philippians 2:9
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:9 states, 'Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him,' reflecting the theme of exaltation above all as in Psalms 57:11.

questions.question: In the historical context of Psalms 57, where was David when he composed this psalm?
options: Fleeing from Saul in a cave
questions.correctAnswer: Fleeing from Saul in a cave
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:1 identifies the setting as when David fled from Saul in the cave, providing the historical context.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'My soul is among lions' in Psalms 57:4 within the ancient Near Eastern cultural context?
options: It symbolizes extreme danger and hostile enemies
It refers to worshiping lion-headed deities
It describes a literal encounter with lions
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes extreme danger and hostile enemies
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, lions symbolized danger and powerful enemies; thus, 'My soul is among lions' (v.4) metaphorically conveys perilous threats.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 57:6 indicates that enemies who set traps for the psalmist ultimately fall into their own pit.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 states, 'They have digged a pit before me, into the midst whereof they are fallen themselves,' showing that the enemies fall into their own trap.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'I will awake early' in Psalms 57:8 suggests the psalmist's intention to rest throughout the day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:8 says, 'I myself will awake early,' indicating eagerness to begin praising God early, not resting during the day.

questions.question: How does Psalms 57:2's description of God as one 'that performeth all things for me' connect with the theme of divine providence in Jeremiah 32:17?
options: Both affirm God's power to accomplish all His purposes
Both focus on God's covenant with Israel
Both emphasize the need for human effort
Both describe God's judgment on nations
questions.correctAnswer: Both affirm God's power to accomplish all His purposes
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:2 praises God as 'that performeth all things for me,' paralleling Jeremiah 32:17's acknowledgment of God's power to create and carry out all plans.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 57 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 57 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted by David when he says, 'for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:1 emphasizes God's mercy as David seeks refuge under God's protective wings, demonstrating trust in divine compassion and protection.

questions.question: What theological truth about God's providence is taught in Psalms 57:2 where David says, 'God that performeth all things for me'?
options: God's sovereign control over all events
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign control over all events
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:2 reveals God's providential governance, showing that God actively performs all things for the believer, affirming divine sovereignty (cf. Romans 8:28).

questions.question: According to Psalms 57:3, what two qualities of God are sent forth to save David from his enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and truth
questions.explanation: Verse 3 explicitly states that God will send forth 'his mercy and his truth' to save David, highlighting these as key attributes in salvation.

questions.question: What does David metaphorically describe his enemies as in Psalms 57:4, and what does this reveal about human sinfulness?
options: Lions with teeth like spears and arrows, showing the destructive nature of sin
Sheep seeking guidance, showing human innocence
Trees rooted in the earth, showing stability
questions.correctAnswer: Lions with teeth like spears and arrows, showing the destructive nature of sin
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:4 portrays enemies as lions with sharp teeth, illustrating the malice and danger posed by human sinfulness and hostility.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by Psalms 57:5, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth'?
options: The doctrine of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's transcendence
questions.explanation: Verse 5 emphasizes God's exaltation above the heavens and earth, teaching His supreme transcendence over all creation.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine justice and human scheming does Psalms 57:6 provide in the metaphor of a net and pit?
options: Those who plot evil against God's people will fall into their own traps
God is unaware of human plans
questions.correctAnswer: Those who plot evil against God's people will fall into their own traps
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 teaches that evil plans against the faithful are ultimately self-defeating as enemies fall into the pits they dig, illustrating divine justice.

questions.question: What aspect of sanctification is reflected in Psalms 57:7 where David declares, 'My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise'?
options: Perseverance in faith and worship despite adversity
questions.correctAnswer: Perseverance in faith and worship despite adversity
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows David's resolved heart to praise God regardless of circumstances, illustrating the sanctified believer's perseverance in faith and worship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 57:8 contribute to the biblical understanding of spiritual worship and dedication?
options: By urging early rising to praise God with musical instruments
questions.correctAnswer: By urging early rising to praise God with musical instruments
questions.explanation: David calls for awakening his glory and instruments early (Psalms 57:8), demonstrating dedication and zeal in worship consistent with biblical praise practices.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:9 teach about the universality of God's praise in redemptive history?
options: God is to be praised among all peoples and nations
God's praise is reserved for Israel only
Praise should be silent and private
questions.correctAnswer: God is to be praised among all peoples and nations
questions.explanation: Verse 9 expresses praise 'among the people' and 'among the nations,' reflecting the biblical theme of universal worship of God (cf. Revelation 5:9).

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness and mercy is conveyed by Psalms 57:3 and Psalms 57:10?
options: God's mercy extends to the heavens and His truth is steadfast, ensuring faithful salvation
God's mercy is limited, and His truth is conditional
God's truth is hidden and uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy extends to the heavens and His truth is steadfast, ensuring faithful salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 10 together show God's mercy and truth as vast and reliable, underpinning His covenant faithfulness to save His people.

questions.question: How do Psalms 57:5-6 and Psalms 57:11 collectively express the doctrine of God's sovereign glory over creation?
options: God is exalted above the heavens and His glory covers all the earth, demonstrating sovereign majesty
God's glory is confined to heaven only
God shares glory with earthly kings
questions.correctAnswer: God is exalted above the heavens and His glory covers all the earth, demonstrating sovereign majesty
questions.explanation: These verses repeatedly declare God's exaltation and glory over all realms, emphasizing His universal sovereignty and majesty.

questions.question: What does Psalms 57:1-3 and Psalms 57:7-9 collectively teach about the believer's response to divine mercy in the midst of trials?
options: Trust in God leads to praise and steadfast worship even during calamities
Believers should despair and avoid worship in trials
Divine mercy means trials will never come
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God leads to praise and steadfast worship even during calamities
questions.explanation: These passages show that trusting God's mercy inspires the believer to praise and fixed-hearted worship despite adversity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine justice is inconsistent because evil seems to prosper temporarily. What does Psalms 57:6 actually teach about the fate of those who plot evil?
options: Those who dig pits for others will fall into them themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Those who dig pits for others will fall into them themselves
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 teaches that evil plots against God's people are self-defeating, as enemies fall into their own traps, affirming consistent divine justice.

questions.question: What Christological foreshadowing is present in Psalms 57:3 where God sends mercy and truth from heaven to save?
options: The sending of the Messiah to provide salvation through mercy and truth
The condemnation of all sinners without mercy
The reliance on human effort for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The sending of the Messiah to provide salvation through mercy and truth
questions.explanation: Verse 3’s depiction of God sending mercy and truth to save prefigures Christ’s incarnation and salvific work (John 1:17).

questions.question: What overarching biblical narrative theme is reflected in David’s refuge in God 'in the shadow of thy wings' during persecution (Psalms 57:1) and his call to praise among nations (Psalms 57:9)?
options: God’s protection of His people leads to universal worship and the restoration of all nations
God’s people are isolated and never praised
God’s mercy is limited to Israel only
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection of His people leads to universal worship and the restoration of all nations
questions.explanation: The refuge imagery coupled with praise among nations reflects the biblical theme of God preserving His people for the global redemption and worship of God (cf. Psalm 22:27).
